answer: An agent market requires each active identity to lock 100 credits for 30 days before it can bid for jobs, and caps each identity at one open bid. Services such as echo, mesa, and opal enforce the same bond rule. An attacker seeking 1,000 simultaneous bids must therefore immobilize 100,000 credits for a month. Creating names is cheap, but each additional bidding slot ties up real capital, making a swarm costly to sustain.
